newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Cooperative NTUC income spends S$70 mln on offices.
newsitem.headline: Cooperative NTUC income spends S$70 mln on offices.

text.p: Cooperative composite insurer NTUC Income said on Saturday it was investing Singapore $70 million in a new out-of-town office building.
Finance for the site is being provided through internal funds, NTUC Income chief executive, Tan Kin Lian, told Reuters at the building's ground-breaking ceremony.
Tan said NTUC Income had an asset base of S$2.7 billion.
"The challenge is to find a good investment, and property is a good investment," he said.
The building, at Tampines Point in eastern Singapore, will be added to existing property holdings of about S$211 million across the Asia-Pacific region, he said.
Work will begin later this month on the 28,000 sq ft site, which was bought for S$40 million in September 1995.
About a third of the company's major functions will be transferred out of central Singapore when the building is completed in May 1998, he said.
